I LOVE AA, and NightMist is my wife's favorite--both are awesome if you can get stuff going. But I'll also admit that though I like the idea of Parse, I've yet to find her useful.  I still try her out sometimes, because I have faith, but I am still waiting to figure out when she shines.

Scouting and manipulating the villain deck does enough 'damage' to the villain, IMO. Against certain villains, it prevents their best stuff from coming out (No Forced Deployments, Dark Heros, Galvanized, or any card that reveals the top H cards of the deck and puts these types of cards into play). Against others, it completely kills their turn (Hey Citizen Dawn, we'll let you play Citizen Spring, no problem! Omnitron, you can totally play that component that gives us an entire round to deal with instead of those blasted flechettes).

Irreucible damage in the right spot can totally turn the tide of the battle as well. Against Apostate, it means you can take out relics of your choosing, like that one that gives all other relics 2DR. Advanced Miss Information with her 2DR is usually annoying, but sometimes one turn of everyone doing irreducible damage to her is all you need to take her out.

She is also one of the few heroes that can destroy ongoings and environments as a power (Omnitron-X and Argent Adept being two other heroes that come to mind). That can save the heroes' collective bacon as well. 

If you want to deal large amounts of damage, then Parse isn't for you. The effect she has on the field isn't readily apparent, but in the right hands, the heroes will have a much easier time fighting the villain with her around.

I can remember once shooting something for about 23 damage after I'd saved up Critical Multiplier stacks for a while and had deliberately done anything other than attack stuff till I could let loose the big hit. I find that's ap retty satisfying thing on Parse - get out all three copies of Critical Multiplier, then play Recompile as often as you can get it and just dump all the Critical Multiplier stacks on someone who can do other things besides hit something every turn, so they can one-shot the last half of the villain's hp away after a few turns or something :D.

The Adept can be effective with just two or three cards out, depending on which ones they are and on the current gameplay situation (ie what kind of abilitis would be useful right now). I had one game against awn where due to constantly having tuff broken I never got out more than two songs and an instrument at any one time, I don't think, yet we managed just fine and I think we won in the end as I kept giving people extra card plays and stuff. Alacritous Subdominant alone, for example, would make Unity very happy and you don't even need any instruments (assuming you're playing the base version of the Adept) :D. In other news, finding out somehere earlier in this thread (I think) a few days ago that the Adept is asexual I thought was pretty cool too - I think I like him even more now :D.

For those who prefer not to play certain characters because they can't really get a grasp on how to play them effectively (or can't really see what kind of use their deck can have), have you ever played in games with other people who do play those characters? It may help you see other ways of playing the character outside of the way you've been trying to play them and you may realise new tricks or methods to them that may make them more enjoyable. Off the top of my head, I think Fanatic and Setback are two that I'm not really a fan of playing too much. It might be because they have a lot of self-harmy stuff and not much by way of reliable healing (unlike, say, Nightmist with Master of Magic and the Starshield Necklace). My partner really likes Redeemer Fanatic, though, so she gets a lot of use during our games :).

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
skoticus:

But I'll also admit that though I like the idea of Parse, I've yet to find her useful.  I still try her out sometimes, because I have faith, but I am still waiting to figure out when she shines.

Try and play her against the Chairman. When you remove every Prison Break from the equasion using Buffer Overlow/Extrasensory Awarness/Updated Intel, make short work of all the villain targets played due to the extra damage from Exploit Vulnerability, and allow your teamates to do crazy things with Syntactic Analysis/Critical Multiplier/Between the Lines, you will learn how truely terrifying her deck is. If she can GUT the Chairman, she can do the same thing to just about any other villain deck.

You have to play Parse with the same mindset you would play Visionary. She is a deck manipulation master, and frankly is much better at it (Visionary brings things like Twist and Mind Control however and DVis has manipulation build in at the base, and while those are much more situational, they are strong in their own right). Maybe doing that or playing that way doesn't seem "glorious" and I can see that being the case. But if you want to talk about the best way to "Win" the game, dictating the entire villain deck to the extent that Parse can strongly flirts with the edge of gamebreakingly powerful.
